newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS END SLIGHTLY DOWN AS BUILDERS RECOVER.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS END SLIGHTLY DOWN AS BUILDERS RECOVER.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed slightly weaker on Wednesday, as a late sudden rally in shares in the debt-ridden construction sector helped to recoup most of the benchmark index's losses, brokers said.
Construction shares were lifted by the news that Mitsui Construction Co Ltd had reached agreement on its restructuring plan with financial institutions, they said.
Wall Street's fall hurt overall sentiment, they added. The 225-share Nikkei average closed the session down 90.51 points or 0.47 percent at 19,008.60. Its September futures fell 70 points to 19,030.
Shares in Japan's property sector 0#REA.T climbed on a media report published on Tuesday about government plans to revise construction laws.
The sector topped the list of percentage gainers, with Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd rising 40 yen to 1,490, Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd 40 yen to 1,690, and Sumitomo Realty & Development Co Ltd 36 yen to 894.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Tuesday that as part of its efforts to revise Japan's building code the government plans to allow landowners to sell rights to unused floor-space allotments for given parcels of land.
